blocking.what: The case analysis gives the result for NaN, ±0 and ±inf, but the last case is written `-X[i]` with the bare minus of ℝ, and the `where` bullet defines it as "the value of the type of $X$ whose magnitude is that of $X[i]$" — the finite case is never stated as the indexed sign change $-_{(\text{f})}X[i]$ of the type of $X$.
blocking.why: Guidelines l.110: a bare `-` is the operation on ℝ; the case analysis of a float section must be written with the indexed operation of the type of the operand, otherwise the finite case is stated in ℝ and not in the floating-point type.
blocking.fix: Write the last case as $-_{(\text{f})}X[i]$ and keep the `where` bullet defining it as the sign change of the type of $X$ (magnitude unchanged, sign reversed), so that every case of the analysis is an operation of the type of $X$.

blocking.what: The case analysis is written with the bare `-X[i]` and the bare `-2^{n-1}`, and the `where` bullet defines `-X[i]` as "the exact negation of the element, the opposite in $\mathbb{Z}$ of the integer $X[i]$, before the reduction modulo $2^n$" — the negation of the signed $n$-bit type is never written as an indexed operation.
blocking.why: Guidelines l.110 and the checklist's per-formula rule: every operation on a machine type is indexed ($-_{(\text{i8})}$, …); a bare `-` denotes the operation on ℝ, so the section as written does not state the machine-type negation it means.
blocking.fix: Write the first case as $-_{(\text{i}n)}X[i]$ (or $-_{(\text{i8})}$, … per type) and define it in the `where` bullet as the negation of the signed $n$-bit type, i.e. the exact negation reduced modulo $2^n$; keep the second case as the value $-2^{n-1}$ of the type.
